newsitem.title: INDIA: Coalition hopes to give Indian shares mild boost.
newsitem.headline: Coalition hopes to give Indian shares mild boost.

text.p: Hopes that India's political leaders are moving closer to forming a new coalition were likely to push shares higher on Tuesday, when the the counry's stock exchanges reopen after a long weekend, brokers said.

Caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, whose government was defeated in a confidence vote on Friday, agreed to step down as leader of the 13-party United Front coalition, raising hopes that the rival Congress party will support a new coalition.

"The (Bombay) market will go up by at least 100/150 points when it opens tomorrow," said Dinesh Valji of stock broking firm Valji Bhimji & Co. But he added the market will probably keep to a narrow range.
On Saturday, the 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange closed 44.01 points down, or 1.21 percent, at 3,589.72.
Hectic parleys in indicated that the Congress Party, which triggered the current political crisis by withdrawing support to Gowda's government, was prepared to support a new combination.
The government's collapse put its fiscal budget for 1997/98 (April/March), acclaimed as India's best-ever, in jeopardy and pushed the country to the brink of a snap poll.
"The passage of the budget is the crucial factor. Marketmen do not want any uncertainty on this count," Valji said.
Brokers said they expected the activity to centre mainly on a few speculative shares which accounted for the bulk of the trading volume of about 5.0 billion rupees on Saturday.
These include Reliance Industries, State Bank of India, Tata Iron and Steel Co, Tata Engineering and Locomotive Co, Associated Cement Companies and ITC.
"Speculators who had gone short will resort to buying," Valji said.
Brokers on Saturday said the markets are expected to rally if a new coalition is cobbled together quickly and investors are assured of some continuity of policies.
"I'm pretty sure a new coalition will be formed," said Ketan Desai, a funds manager at brokerage Asit C. Mehta Investment Intermediates Ltd. "The market's cautiously optimistic."
Holding the markets together was the promise that the budget would be approved by parliament in a special April 21-23 session, analysts said.
"Once the budget is passed the market will slide," said Rajesh Bajaj, director at Calcutta brokerage Lohia Securities.
A fractious mandate in last year's national elections gave no single party or group a majority.
The United Front has 178 members, the Congress 140 and the right-wing Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its allies 193 in the 545-member Lok Sabha, or lower house of parliament.
